::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## How this was made
The derivations, the prose and the code for every demo were drafted by Claude, an AI model made by Anthropic, in conversation with me. This is a first version and has not yet been checked line by line.
:::

Every instrument in this series is worked out the same way, in three steps.

1. **Operator.** Apply Newton's law to a small piece of the instrument. The restoring force per unit mass, written as a function of the shape, is an operator $\mathcal{L}$, and the motion obeys $u_{tt} = -\mathcal{L}u$. The supports give the boundary conditions.
2. **Spectrum.** Each eigenpair $\mathcal{L}X = \omega^2 X$ is a standing wave $X(x)\cos\omega t$. The eigenvalues fix which frequencies the instrument can make.
3. **Sound.** How you play it, by bow, reed, hammer, thumb or stick, fixes how strongly each mode is excited. Whether the frequencies line up on whole-number multiples decides whether you hear a pitch.

## Hear them side by side

Gray lines are whole-number multiples of the fundamental. Stem height is how strongly each partial is excited.

## Reading path

| Part | Instrument | Operator | What you can play |
|:-----|:-----------|:---------|:------------------|
| 0 | [Foundations](foundations.qmd) | $m\ddot u_j = \tfrac{T}{h}(u_{j+1}-2u_j+u_{j-1}) \to c^2u_{xx}$ | beads on a thread |
| 1 | [Violin](violin.qmd) | $-c^2\partial_x^2$ | a bowed fingerboard |
| 2 | [Clarinet](clarinet.qmd) | $-c^2\partial_x^2$, with $p_x = 0$ at the reed | tone holes and a register key |
| 3 | [Kalimba](kalimba.qmd) | $\kappa^2\partial_x^4$ | seventeen tines |
| 4 | [Piano](piano.qmd) | $-c^2\partial_x^2 + \kappa^2\partial_x^4$ | a keyboard with a stiffness knob |
| 5 | [Drum](drum.qmd) | $-c^2\Delta$ | a drumhead you strike anywhere |

## Comparison

| | Violin | Clarinet | Kalimba | Piano | Drum |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| Restoring force | tension | air pressure | bending stiffness | tension + bending | tension, in 2D |
| Newton's law on | a segment | a slab of air | a slice: torque, then force | a segment, both forces added | a patch, via the divergence theorem |
| Operator | $-c^2\partial_x^2$ | $-c^2\partial_x^2$ on pressure | $\kappa^2\partial_x^4$ | $-c^2\partial_x^2+\kappa^2\partial_x^4$ | $-c^2\Delta$ |
| Boundary | $u=0$ at both ends | $p_x=0$ at reed, $p=0$ at open end | $u=u'=0$ at clamp, $u''=u'''=0$ at tip | $u=u''=0$ at both ends | $u=0$ on the rim |
| Eigen-condition | $\sin kL=0$ | $\cos kL=0$ | $\cos\beta L\cosh\beta L=-1$ | $\sin kL=0$ | $J_m(ka)=0$ |
| $f_n/f_1$ | $n$ | $2n-1$ | $(\beta_n/\beta_1)^2$: 1, 6.27, 17.5 | $n\sqrt{(1+Bn^2)/(1+B)}$ | $j_{m,n}/j_{0,1}$: 1, 1.59, 2.14 |
| Excitation | bow, sustained | reed, sustained | thumb pluck | felt hammer | stick |
| Why it sounds as it does | periodic: exact harmonics | periodic, odd harmonics dominate: overblows a twelfth | overtones weak, far and brief: pitch survives | near-harmonic: pitch, stretched octaves | inharmonic and long-lived: a thud |

```{=html}
<script src="core.js"></script>
<script>
(function () {
  "use strict";
  var C = Core, M = C.models;
  var DEF = {
    violin: function () { return M.violin.partials(); },
    kalimba: function () { return M.kalimba.partials(); },
    piano: function () { return M.piano.partials({ B: 0.0012 }); },
    drum: function () { return M.drum.partials({ r: 0.35 }); },
    clarinet: function () { return M.clarinet.partials(); }
  };
  function draw() {
    document.querySelectorAll("svg[data-mini]").forEach(function (svg) {
      C.stems(svg, DEF[svg.getAttribute("data-mini")](), { W: 200, H: 58, rmax: 8, fs: 9, sw: 2, labelEvery: 2 });
    });
    document.querySelectorAll("[data-ratios]").forEach(function (td) {
      td.textContent = DEF[td.getAttribute("data-ratios")]().map(function (p) { return p.ratio; }).sort(function (a, b) { return a - b; }).slice(0, 5).map(function (r) { return r.toFixed(2); }).join(", ");
    });
  }
  function fadeOut(buf, sec) { var d = buf.getChannelData(0), n = Math.floor(sec * buf.sampleRate); for (var i = 0; i < n; i++) d[d.length - 1 - i] *= i / n; return buf; }
  document.querySelectorAll("[data-play]").forEach(function (b) {
    b.addEventListener("click", function () {
      var id = b.getAttribute("data-play"), f = M[id].F0, buf;
      if (id === "violin" || id === "clarinet") buf = fadeOut(C.render(C.toHz(DEF[id](), f), 1.8), 0.4);
      else buf = C.render(C.toHz(DEF[id](), f), id === "piano" ? 3.2 : 2.6);
      C.play(buf, 0.8);
    });
  });
  C.onTheme(draw);
  draw();
})();
</script>
```
